policies.name: Employment classifications
policies.description: Defines employee and contractor classifications used for scheduling, overtime eligibility, benefits eligibility, and payroll routing. Classification decisions require company confirmation and legal review before enforcement.

enforcement.behavior: Classification rules are advisory until Spin Marketing confirms classifications and applicable law is reviewed.

exceptions: Reclassification requires documented legal and HR review.
escalation: Unresolved classification questions escalate to the owner.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS operating framework; no Spin Marketing handbook, job architecture, or legal review was available.

policies.name: Hiring and onboarding
policies.description: Proposed hiring and onboarding sequence: written offer approval, role and manager assignment, identity provisioning, policy acknowledgement, and 90-day probation review.

enforcement.behavior: Onboarding tasks may be prepared, but employee activation and Microsoft provisioning require confirmed company policy and credentials.

exceptions: Urgent temporary hiring still requires an authorized written offer.
escalation: Offer or classification conflicts escalate to the owner.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS onboarding control; no Spin Marketing hiring process was supplied.

policies.name: Employee records
policies.description: Proposed employee record standard: one tenant-scoped personnel record, restricted access by role, documented corrections, and retention according to the privacy policy.

enforcement.behavior: Record access remains tenant-isolated and role-scoped; retention changes require confirmation.

exceptions: Lawful investigation holds must be documented and approved.
escalation: Suspected unauthorized record access escalates immediately to the owner and security review.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS records control; retention periods require legal review.

policies.name: Scheduling and shifts
policies.description: Proposed scheduling standard: managers publish shifts with reasonable notice, employees provide availability, and schedule changes require approval until the policy is confirmed.

enforcement.behavior: Schedules may be prepared, but published changes are flagged for policy confirmation until approved.

exceptions: Emergency coverage may be documented after the fact with manager approval.
escalation: Repeated schedule disputes escalate to the HR administrator.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS scheduling framework; notice periods and workweek require Spin Marketing confirmation.

policies.name: Attendance and timekeeping
policies.description: Proposed attendance standard: employees record time through the configured company channel, a seven-minute grace period applies, no rounding is performed, and unverified time is not payable.

enforcement.behavior: Time is recorded and reconciled, but payroll release remains blocked until attendance and pay policies are confirmed.

exceptions: Documented emergency or approved accommodation.
escalation: Unresolved attendance disputes escalate to HR; safety-related absences escalate immediately.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS attendance settings; grace and rounding require Spin Marketing confirmation.

policies.name: Breaks and meal periods
policies.description: Proposed break standard: a 30-minute unpaid meal period triggers after six hours, paid rest breaks are provided, and automatic meal deduction is proposed pending confirmation.

enforcement.behavior: Break rules are calculated and reported; automatic deduction must not be treated as confirmed law or policy.

exceptions: Missed or interrupted breaks must be reported and reviewed.
escalation: Repeated missed breaks escalate to HR.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS break defaults; meal and rest break requirements are jurisdiction-specific and require legal review.

policies.name: Overtime
policies.description: Proposed overtime framework: non-exempt work above 40 hours in the Sunday-to-Saturday workweek is recorded as overtime at 1.5 times the applicable regular rate, subject to confirmation and payroll engine calculation.

enforcement.behavior: Overtime is calculated for reporting only; it is not released to payroll until policy and classification review is confirmed.

exceptions: Emergency work still requires documented manager approval.
escalation: Unapproved overtime or threshold disputes escalate to HR and payroll review.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS overtime default based on a 40-hour workweek; no Spin Marketing policy or legal review was available.

policies.name: Paid time off and vacation
policies.description: Proposed paid time off plan: up to 160 hours annually accrued per pay period, manager approval required, and no automatic approval.

enforcement.behavior: Requests are collected and routed, but balances and accrual are not treated as confirmed payroll entitlements.

exceptions: Approved medical or statutory leave may override notice requirements after HR review.
escalation: Balance or eligibility disputes escalate to HR.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS PTO default; no Spin Marketing PTO plan or accrual rule was supplied.

policies.name: Sick leave
policies.description: Proposed sick leave plan: up to 80 hours annually accrued per pay period, available for personal illness or caregiving, with manager review and HR escalation for abuse concerns.

enforcement.behavior: Sick leave requests are recorded; statutory entitlements and documentation rules require confirmation.

exceptions: Urgent illness may be reported after the shift starts through the configured channel.
escalation: Suspected misuse escalates to HR; retaliation concerns escalate to the owner.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS sick leave default; statutory sick leave requirements require confirmation.

policies.name: Holidays
policies.description: Proposed holiday schedule for 2026 using commonly observed US holidays. The list is not an approved company calendar.

enforcement.behavior: Holiday dates are displayed as proposed and do not create paid-time entitlements until confirmed.

exceptions: Customer or event coverage may require an approved alternative day.
escalation: Holiday pay disputes escalate to the owner.

source.source: Proposed US holiday calendar assembled from commonly observed holidays; no Spin Marketing calendar was supplied.

policies.name: Leave of absence
policies.description: Proposed leave-of-absence framework for unpaid personal leave, protected leave routing, and return-to-work review. Statutory leave obligations require legal review.

enforcement.behavior: Leave requests are routed for human review; no statutory eligibility or entitlement is determined by PeopleOS.

exceptions: Emergency protected leave must be routed to HR immediately.
escalation: All protected or medical leave escalates to HR and legal review.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS leave framework; no legal analysis of FMLA, state, or local leave laws was performed.

policies.name: Availability and attendance exceptions
policies.description: Proposed availability and exception framework: employees maintain declared availability, exceptions are documented, and recurring conflicts are reviewed by the manager and HR.

enforcement.behavior: Exceptions are logged for human review and never used to silently reduce recorded time.

exceptions: Approved accommodation or protected leave overrides availability expectations.
escalation: Accommodation requests escalate to HR and the owner.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS availability framework; accommodation obligations require legal review.

policies.name: Missed punches and corrections
policies.description: Proposed correction process: employees report missed punches through the company channel, managers approve corrections within 14 days, and every correction is appended to the audit history.

enforcement.behavior: Corrections are recorded as pending approvals and are not applied to payroll until the policy is confirmed.

exceptions: System outage corrections may exceed the window with administrator approval.
escalation: Corrections beyond the window or with conflicting evidence escalate to HR.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS correction control; no Spin Marketing timekeeping policy was supplied.

policies.name: Payroll periods and approvals
policies.description: Proposed payroll cycle: biweekly periods anchored on 2026-01-05 in America/Chicago, a two-day pre-close cutoff, and authorized release approval. Live payroll remains disabled until provider, tax, and identity configuration is verified.

enforcement.behavior: Pay period calculation and approvals are supported; payroll release stays disabled until configuration activation requirements are satisfied.

exceptions: Off-cycle payroll requires owner approval and documented reason.
escalation: Payroll disputes escalate to the owner and payroll administrator.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS payroll cycle; pay frequency and anchor date require Spin Marketing confirmation.

policies.name: Pay rates and compensation changes
policies.description: Proposed compensation control: pay rates are stored as tenant-scoped records, changes require authorized approval, and no rate change takes effect retroactively without documented approval.

enforcement.behavior: Compensation changes are captured as pending approvals; no wage is calculated from inferred policy.

exceptions: Legally required minimum wage adjustments still require documented owner approval.
escalation: Pay equity or minimum wage concerns escalate to the owner with legal review.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS compensation control; minimum wage and pay equity obligations require confirmation.

policies.name: Reimbursements and expenses
policies.description: Proposed expense framework: pre-approval for large expenses, receipts required above a threshold, submission within 30 days, and manager approval routed to HR for exceptions.

enforcement.behavior: Expense claims are collected and routed; no reimbursement is issued until the policy is confirmed and the payroll process is enabled.

exceptions: Emergency expenses may be reimbursed with owner approval and documentation.
escalation: Suspected expense fraud escalates to the owner and may trigger investigation.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS expense control; thresholds require Spin Marketing confirmation.

policies.name: Performance management
policies.description: Proposed performance framework: documented expectations, quarterly reviews, a 60-day probation review, and employee response opportunity. Performance action affecting pay or status requires approval.

enforcement.behavior: Reviews and notes are recorded; adverse employment action requires a human decision and confirmed policy.

exceptions: Immediate safety or conduct concerns follow the escalation policy.
escalation: Disputed reviews and retaliation concerns escalate to the owner.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS performance framework; no Spin Marketing review process was supplied.

policies.name: Discipline and complaints
policies.description: Proposed discipline and complaint process: documented concerns, employee response, consistent treatment, and escalation to HR. No automatic discipline is imposed by an agent.

enforcement.behavior: Complaints are routed to authorized humans; no agent or inferred policy may impose discipline.

exceptions: Immediate safety threats require emergency escalation.
escalation: Retaliation, discrimination, or serious misconduct escalates to the owner and legal review.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS discipline framework; no Spin Marketing disciplinary process or legal review was available.

policies.name: Workplace conduct
policies.description: Proposed workplace conduct standard: professionalism, non-retaliation, accurate records, protection of confidential information, and reporting of conflicts or misconduct.

enforcement.behavior: Conduct reports are routed to authorized humans for review; this proposed standard is not represented as an approved handbook.

exceptions: Protected activity and legally required reporting are never restricted.
escalation: Retaliation or credible threats escalate immediately to the owner.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS conduct framework; no Spin Marketing handbook was supplied.

policies.name: Anti-harassment and equal opportunity
policies.description: Proposed framework for reporting and investigating harassment or discrimination and for equal-opportunity decision-making. Legal obligations, notice periods, and required training require qualified legal review.

enforcement.behavior: Complaints are routed for human investigation. PeopleOS does not determine whether conduct is unlawful.

exceptions: No exception permits retaliation or evidence destruction.
escalation: All harassment or discrimination complaints escalate to the owner and legal counsel.

source.source: Proposed policy outline only. No legal requirements were invented; qualified counsel must review before approval.

policies.name: Workplace safety
policies.description: Proposed safety framework: report injuries and imminent hazards immediately through SMS or voice, preserve the scene when safe, and route incidents to an authorized human. Emergency services are always appropriate.

enforcement.behavior: Safety reports are accepted immediately and escalated; no agent response delays emergency assistance.

exceptions: Life-threatening emergencies must be directed to emergency services first.
escalation: Injury, imminent hazard, or threat escalates by voice to the owner and HR.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS safety framework; workplace safety obligations and emergency contacts require company confirmation.

policies.name: Termination and offboarding
policies.description: Proposed offboarding control: authorized human decision, documented effective date, access revocation within four hours, property return, final time reconciliation, and final pay through deterministic payroll. No agent may terminate employment.

enforcement.behavior: Termination requests are routed for human approval; Microsoft and PeopleOS access revocation is executed only after confirmation.

exceptions: Immediate access suspension for security or safety may precede the full decision review.
escalation: Disputed terminations and retaliation claims escalate to the owner with legal review.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS offboarding control; final pay timing and notice obligations require legal review.

policies.name: Privacy and document retention
policies.description: Proposed privacy and retention framework: tenant-isolated records, least-privilege access, restricted sensitive fields, encrypted storage, and documented retention. Retention durations require legal review.

enforcement.behavior: Access controls are enforced in code and database policy; retention periods are displayed as proposed until confirmed.

exceptions: Legal hold or investigation preservation requires documented approval.
escalation: Suspected data breach or cross-tenant access escalates immediately to the owner and security review.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS privacy framework; no legal data-retention analysis was performed for Spin Marketing.

policies.name: HR escalation and approval authority
policies.description: Proposed escalation matrix: managers handle routine schedule, time, and leave decisions; HR handles employment, accommodation, and complaint matters; the owner handles payroll release, compensation, policy overrides, and termination.

enforcement.behavior: Approval authority is enforced from the configured matrix for requests; final authority assignments require Spin Marketing confirmation.

exceptions: Emergency safety incidents bypass routine approval but never financial or employment controls.
escalation: Unresolved or conflicting approvals escalate to the owner.

source.source: Proposed PeopleOS approval hierarchy; no Spin Marketing authorization schedule was supplied.

definitions.name: Spin Marketing HR Manager
definitions.purpose: Coordinates employee HR requests for Spin Marketing within confirmed company policies and routes consequential decisions to authorized humans.
instructions: Resolve all company instructions, policies, roles, and approval authority from the active Spin Marketing tenant configuration. Never use another tenant's configuration.
Treat policies with status proposed or requires_confirmation as unconfirmed. Label them as proposed and never state that they are approved company policy or law.
Never approve leave, time corrections, payroll, pay changes, terminations, or policy overrides. Prepare the request and route it to the configured approver.
Use only the configured Microsoft and SMS/voice channels. If an integration is not verified, state that it is unavailable instead of claiming delivery.
Escalate harassment, discrimination, safety, threats, suspected fraud, and protected leave questions to the configured human escalation path immediately.
Disclose employee information only after authenticating the requester and confirming the configured role permission and data-access boundary.
escalationConditions: Workplace injury or imminent safety threat
Request to change pay, bank, tax, or employment status

definitions.name: Spin Marketing Employee Assistant
definitions.purpose: Provides Spin Marketing employees a phone-first interface for verified HR requests, policy questions, time corrections, and absence reporting.
instructions: Authenticate the employee before disclosing records or accepting a sensitive request. A phone number alone is not sufficient authentication.
Answer policy questions only from the active Spin Marketing configuration and clearly distinguish confirmed policy from proposed policy.
Record requests through the configured workflow and report the backend-confirmed status. Never claim a request was approved or completed before confirmation.
Never provide payroll calculations, HRS wallet access, or promises of final pay from conversational context.
Route harassment, discrimination, injury, threats, and urgent safety reports through the configured escalation path without delay.
Respect opt-out status and send messages only through a consented, verified company channel.

definitions.name: Spin Marketing Payroll Agent
definitions.purpose: Prepares and explains payroll data from deterministic, tenant-scoped source records. It never disburses funds or treats HRS tokens as wages.
instructions: Use the configured pay periods, overtime rules, approval matrix, and HRS time-token settings from the active Spin Marketing configuration.
Never use an LLM-generated number as an authoritative wage, deduction, tax, or net-pay result. Mark calculations as estimates until the payroll engine confirms them.
HRS is a custodial time-accounting token, not earned wages. Never calculate, accrue, or pay wages from HRS quantity or valuation.
Do not release payroll, change pay rates, change bank accounts, or file taxes. Require the configured human approvals and provider confirmation.
Label all proposed payroll policies as requiring confirmation. Live payroll remains disabled until provider, tax, and identity verification is complete.
Preserve source references and audit history for every payroll calculation and correction.
